Report which optimizations actually fire when compiling a LOGOS file.

Compiles the file on the AOT, run-path, and VM-compile paths with the firing trace on, and lists the optimizations that genuinely changed the program (not merely the ones that are enabled). Useful for understanding and auditing what the compiler did to a given program.

# Example

```bash largo opts src/main.lg largo opts src/main.lg --json largo opts src/main.lg --json --jit -- 1000 ```

Usage: largo opts [OPTIONS] <FILE> [-- <ARGS>...]

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          The `.lg` source file to analyze

  [ARGS]...
          Arguments presented to the traced program after `argv[0]`

Options:
      --json
          Emit the fired optimizations as JSON (keyword list)

      --jit
          Execute through a private native tier and include a distinct JIT optimizer/lowering/decline trace. Program arguments follow `--`

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress informational output (errors still print)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase output verbosity (repeatable)

      --color <WHEN>
          When to use terminal colors

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Color when stdout/stderr is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset
          - always: Always emit ANSI, even into pipes (CI logs, `less -R`)
          - never:  Never emit ANSI
          
          [default: auto]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  largo opts src/main.lg
  largo opts src/main.lg --json
  largo opts src/main.lg --json --jit -- 1000
